Awe is not a proof checker
Feeling intellectually overwhelmed by Jaynes is evidence about the reader’s experience. It is not evidence that every argument is flawless. Halpern’s counterexample to formulations of Cox-style representation results illustrates why assumptions deserve inspection even in beautiful foundational arguments; probability theory itself survives that inspection.
Halpern (1999)

The psychometric threshold is a guess
The author labels this estimate speculative. There is no measurement here establishing how much intelligence separates recognizing an achievement from producing it, or a universal cutoff beyond which readers cannot discriminate quality. Turning the guess into a hierarchy of whose judgments count would compound its uncertainty.

A career deadline is not a cognitive law
The imagined need to catch up by a particular age gives the narrative urgency without establishing a general limit on contribution. Research combines specialized knowledge, collaboration, tools and complementary abilities. A person’s worth or scientific usefulness cannot be inferred from whether they outrank a chosen genius on an unspecified scale.
